rows.stem: Many copepods live on the body surface of marine fish. This relationship is an example of :
rows.solution: Copepods living on the body surface of marine fish are **ectoparasites**: they feed on the host (its skin, mucus or body fluids) and harm it, while they themselves benefit. NCERT gives this exact example: many marine fish are infested with ectoparasitic copepods. An interaction in which one species benefits and the other is harmed is **parasitism**. So the answer is option (B) Parasitism.

rows.stem:
Given below are structural details of a human mammary gland :
(i) The glandular tissue in the breast has 15-20 clusters of cells called alveoli.
(ii) The milk is stored in the lumen of alveoli.
(iii) The alveoli join to form the mammary ducts.
(iv) Mammary ampulla is connected to lactiferous ducts.
Choose the option that gives the correct detail of human mammary gland.
rows.solution:
Check each statement against the structure of the mammary gland:
- (i) is incorrect: the glandular tissue of each breast is divided into **15-20 mammary lobes**, and it is these lobes that contain clusters of cells called alveoli.
- (ii) is correct: the cells of the alveoli secrete milk, which is **stored in the cavities (lumens) of the alveoli**.
- (iii) is incorrect: the alveoli open into **mammary tubules**, and it is the tubules of each lobe that join to form a mammary duct.
- (iv) is correct: several mammary ducts join to form a wider **mammary ampulla**, which is connected to the **lactiferous duct** through which milk is sucked out.

So the answer is option (C) (ii) and (iv).

rows.stem: Tetanus antitoxin (Tetanus toxoid) when injected into the human body it immediately provides :
rows.solution:
An antitoxin is a preparation of **preformed antibodies** against the tetanus toxin. When such ready-made antibodies are injected, the body gets protection at once without producing antibodies of its own, which is **passive immunity**. This is why a person suspected of tetanus infection is given an antitoxin for a quick response.

Note that a tetanus **toxoid** (inactivated toxin) works differently: it makes the body produce its own antibodies, which gives active immunity and takes time to build up. The stem's word "immediately" and the antitoxin it describes point to passive immunity. So the answer is option (B) Passive immunity.

rows.stem: The sixth extinction in progress currently is different from all previous extinctions on earth as it is :
rows.solution: The IUCN Red List shows that species are being lost much faster now than in earlier times. The current, **sixth extinction** differs from the five earlier episodes in two ways: it is caused largely by **human activities**, and its rate is far higher. Current species extinction rates are estimated to be **100 to 1,000 times faster** than in pre-human times. So the answer is option (B) 100-1000 times faster.

rows.stem:
(a) Name (i) a GM cereal crop having enhanced nutritional value, (ii) the nutrient it is rich in.
(b) State any two benefits of Genetically modified crops.
rows.solution:
(a)
- (i) **Golden rice**, a genetically modified variety of rice.
- (ii) It is rich in **vitamin A** (it produces beta-carotene, the precursor of vitamin A).

(b) Any two benefits of genetically modified crops:
- **Tolerance to abiotic stresses** such as cold, drought, salt and heat.
- **Reduced reliance on chemical pesticides** because of pest-resistant crops (for example Bt cotton).
- **Reduced post-harvest losses**.
- **Increased efficiency of mineral usage** by plants, which prevents early exhaustion of soil fertility.
- **Enhanced nutritional value** of food (for example vitamin A enriched rice).
- Creation of **tailor-made plants** that supply alternative resources such as starches, fuels and pharmaceuticals to industry.

rows.stem:
Certain specific bacterial spores are mixed in water and sprayed over Brassica crop to control butterfly catterpillars.
Name this bacterium and its mode of action on the butterfly catterpillars.
rows.solution:
The bacterium is **Bacillus thuringiensis** (Bt).

Its mode of action on the butterfly caterpillars:
- The dried spores of the bacterium, mixed with water, are sprayed on vulnerable plants such as Brassica and fruit trees, where they are **eaten by the caterpillars**.
- The bacterium produces a toxin as an **inactive protoxin**. In the **gut of the larva the toxin is released and activated**: the alkaline pH of the gut solubilises the crystals.
- The activated toxin binds to the surface of the midgut epithelial cells and creates pores, causing the cells to swell and lyse, so the **larva gets killed**. The other insects are left unharmed, which is why Bt is a specific biocontrol agent.

rows.stem:
Immunotherapy these days is one of the most efficient way of treatment of cancer. The therapy involved activates the immune system and destroys the tumour.
(i) Write an example of one such biological response modifier used in immunotherapy.
(ii) Why do patients need such substances if immune system is already working in body ?
(iii) State what is 'Contact inhibition'.
rows.solution:
- (i) **\(\alpha\)-interferon** is a biological response modifier used in immunotherapy.
- (ii) Tumour cells are able to **avoid detection and destruction by the immune system**, so the body's own immune system does not act against them. Biological response modifiers such as \(\alpha\)-interferon **activate the immune system** and help it to destroy the tumour.
- (iii) **Contact inhibition** is the property of normal cells by virtue of which **contact with other cells inhibits their uncontrolled growth**. Cancer cells have lost this property, so they continue to divide and form a mass of cells called a tumour.

rows.stem:
"Some species of insects and frogs have evolved with various specific features that help them from being detected."
(a) Justify the statement giving reasons.
(b) Mention any two such features.
rows.solution:
(a) Prey species have evolved various defences to **lessen the impact of predation**. If an insect or frog could not avoid its predators, it would be eaten and the prey population could be driven to extinction. Features that keep the animal from being detected, or that make it unattractive to a predator, therefore **protect the individual and help the species survive**.

(b) Any two such features:
- **Camouflage**: some species of insects and frogs are **cryptically coloured**, so they blend with their surroundings and are not easily detected by the predator.
- **Poisonous or distasteful body**: some animals are poisonous and therefore avoided by predators (for example, the Monarch butterfly is distasteful because of a special chemical present in its body, acquired by feeding on a poisonous weed during its caterpillar stage).

rows.stem: Mention Darwin's observations made on finches during his visit to Galapagos Islands. Write the explanation given by Darwin on his observations.
rows.solution:
**Darwin's observations** on his visit to the Galapagos Islands:
- He observed an amazing **diversity of small black birds (Darwin's finches)** living on the islands.
- Many varieties of finches were found on the **same island**, and they differed mainly in the **shape and size of their beaks**.
- He realised that the original finches were **seed-eaters**, and that **altered beaks arose** among them, enabling some to become **insectivorous** and others vegetarian (feeding on cactus, fruits and so on).

**His explanation**: all these varieties had evolved from a common ancestral seed-eating finch on the island itself. As the finches spread to different habitats, they adapted to the different food available there, and their beaks changed accordingly. This process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area, starting from a point and radiating to other areas of habitat, is called **adaptive radiation**, and it led to the formation of new species (speciation).

rows.stem: "RNA interference has been used to produce transgenic tobacco plants to protect them from the infestation by specific nematodes." Explain the novel strategy exploited by the biotechnologists.
rows.solution:
A nematode, Meloidogyne incognita, infects the roots of tobacco plants and causes a great reduction in yield. Biotechnologists used **RNA interference (RNAi)** to protect the plant:
- RNAi is a method of **cellular defence** found in all eukaryotes, in which a specific mRNA is **silenced** by a complementary double stranded RNA (dsRNA) that binds to it and prevents its translation.
- Using **Agrobacterium vectors**, **nematode-specific genes** were introduced into the host (tobacco) plant.
- The introduced DNA was such that it produced **both sense and antisense RNA** in the host cells.
- These two RNAs, being complementary to each other, formed a **double stranded RNA (dsRNA)**, which initiated RNAi.
- The dsRNA **silenced the specific mRNA of the nematode**.
- As a result the parasite **could not survive** in a transgenic host expressing the specific interfering RNA, so the transgenic plant was protected from the nematode.

rows.stem:
(i) How and why is charging of tRNA essential in the process of translation ?
(ii) State the function of ribosome as a catalyst in bacteria during the process of translation.
(iii) Explain the process of binding of ribosomal units to mRNA during protein synthesis.
rows.solution:
(i) **Charging of tRNA (aminoacylation)**:
- **How**: each amino acid is **activated in the presence of ATP** and linked to its **cognate tRNA**. The tRNA carrying its amino acid is called a charged tRNA.
- **Why it is essential**: the charged tRNA reads the codon on the mRNA through its anticodon and brings the correct amino acid to it. When two charged tRNAs are brought close enough, the formation of a **peptide bond between their amino acids is favoured energetically**, because the energy used to charge them is now available for the bond. Without charging, amino acids could neither be placed according to the code nor joined.

(ii) In bacteria the **23S rRNA** of the ribosome acts as the enzyme (a **ribozyme**) for the formation of peptide bonds. The ribosome therefore acts as a catalyst that **enhances the rate of peptide bond formation** between the amino acids during translation.

(iii) **Binding of the ribosomal units to mRNA**:
- In its inactive state the ribosome exists as **two subunits**, a large subunit and a small subunit.
- When the **small subunit encounters an mRNA**, the process of translation begins: the start codon (AUG) is recognised by the charged initiator tRNA.
- The **large subunit** then joins. It has **two sites** to which subsequent amino acids (on their charged tRNAs) bind, bringing them close enough to each other for the **formation of a peptide bond**.
- The ribosome moves from codon to codon along the mRNA, adding amino acids one by one, until a stop codon is reached and the ribosome is released.

rows.stem: Describe the dihybrid cross upto \(\text{F}_2\) generation as conducted by Gregor Mendel using pure lines of Garden Pea for characters seed shape and seed colour.
rows.solution:
Mendel crossed two pure lines of garden pea differing in two characters: seed shape (round, R, dominant over wrinkled, r) and seed colour (yellow, Y, dominant over green, y).

**Parental (P) generation**: round yellow (RRYY) \(\times\) wrinkled green (rryy).

**Gametes**: the round yellow parent forms only RY gametes; the wrinkled green parent forms only ry gametes.

**\(\text{F}_1\) generation**: all plants are RrYy, with **round yellow** seeds.

**Selfing of \(\text{F}_1\)** (RrYy \(\times\) RrYy): because the two pairs of alleles segregate independently, each \(\text{F}_1\) plant forms four kinds of gametes, RY, Ry, rY and ry, in equal proportion (1/4 each).

**\(\text{F}_2\) generation** (Punnett square):

| Gametes | RY | Ry | rY | ry |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RY | RRYY | RRYy | RrYY | RrYy |
| Ry | RRYy | RRyy | RrYy | Rryy |
| rY | RrYY | RrYy | rrYY | rrYy |
| ry | RrYy | Rryy | rrYy | rryy |

**\(\text{F}_2\) phenotypic ratio**: **9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green**.

From such dihybrid crosses Mendel proposed the **law of independent assortment**: when two pairs of traits are combined in a hybrid, the segregation of one pair of characters is independent of the other pair of characters.
